note: Wave status the deck reads. Written by the orchestrator when an agent is launched and when it reports. The deck shows the `asOf` stamp rather than implying live polling — a published page cannot see this session, and pretending otherwise is the same failure as a screen rendering a total it did not compute.
waveNote: The critical path. Ten product agents idle until these contracts are stable.

agents.name: Integration & Release
agents.scope: CI pipeline, shared-file arbitration, re-verifying each agent's Definition of Done before anything merges
blocks: every merge to main — no agent merges its own branch
agents.notes: CI only runs checks that exist. Suites still being built are absent rather than stubbed green; a job reporting success without running anything is the CI equivalent of a screen rendering a total it did not compute.

agents.name: UI Foundation
agents.scope: Modal system (6 variants, focus trap, mobile sheet), Form system over Zod, Charts extracted from accounting/Reports.tsx, state kit

agents.name: Backend & Data
agents.scope: Fastify + Drizzle schema + RLS + migrations, seed from the existing fixtures, core entity routes with server-side RBAC and audit, repository mutations and httpRepository
blocks: every capability's Definition of Done — real data, persistence and audit are clauses in it
agents.notes: Postgres may not be available in this container; schema, migrations, RLS and seed are still written in full and anything unverifiable is reported rather than faked.

agents.name: Test Infrastructure
agents.scope: vitest + jsdom + testing-library, RBAC unit tests across 14 roles × 28 modules × 5 actions, FIELD_RULES reachability audit, component tests, registry-driven route coverage in smoke.mjs

agents.name: Auth & Security
agents.scope: JWT with rotating refresh and reuse detection, argon2id, session revocation, OTP throttling, server-side RBAC middleware, tenant and branch isolation tests
blocks: G10 portals — separate audiences need a session model
agents.notes: Held until agent 05 lands the server scaffold. The plan runs all four concurrently, but auth builds on the server it authenticates: launching both into server/** at once is exactly the shared-file contention the ownership rule exists to prevent.

shared.note: package.json was updated by the orchestrator before launch — vitest, testing-library, jsdom, msw and zod are installed, and the test scripts added — so no agent needs to touch it. That file is the top contention point in the plan.
